source.title: Two Stages of Folding: Convergent Mechanisms in AI Protein Folding Trunks
source.authors: K. Lu; Jannik Brinkmann; S. Huber; Aaron Mueller; Yonatan Belinkov; David Bau; C. Wendler

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model representational alignment and transfer in protein-folding models using CKA, whitened Procrustes projections, and activation patching; it does not test the original claim’s scale trend.
record.gate_note: The study reports cross-model similarity, linear alignment, shuffled-correspondence controls, and functional substitution by cross-model patching. Other mechanistic results about charge and distance features do not directly measure the claim’s cross-model convergence.
record.test_reason: The study maps pairwise representations between three independently trained protein-folding trunks (ESMFold, OpenFold, Boltz-1). It uses CKA, whitened Procrustes with shuffled-correspondence controls, and cross-model activation patching. This tests V4 (linear interchangeability) in a new domain. It is better classed as T3 (new setting with a result on the claim) than T2: the authors present it as Platonic-hypothesis evidence beyond vision and language, and there is no scale sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that ESMFold, OpenFold and Boltz-1 share a two-stage organization. They find middle and late pairwise representations are linearly alignable and functionally interchangeable at the corresponding stage, despite different architectures, inputs and training. They explicitly present this as Platonic-hypothesis evidence in a domain beyond vision and language.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CKA, whitened Procrustes, and causal cross-model patching on protein-folding trunks rather than testing alignment growth with model scale or capability.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment and transfer vary by model pairing; ESMFold–OpenFold aligns more strongly than pairings involving Boltz-1. Cross-model patching success is asymmetric by transfer direction.

fits_no_version.finding: All three trunks share a two-stage organization: early seq2pair write-in of charge, then late pairwise distance encoding (probe R2 ≈ 0.9). Steering charge or distance directions induces hairpins in each model. The concepts are probed per model, not matched across models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained models of a domain recover the same supervised-probe concepts and the same processing stages at corresponding depths.

record.problems: Only three protein-folding models are compared. The study does not vary model scale or capability, does not test vision-language alignment, and does not identify whether shared training data/objectives or a common model of reality explains the observed alignment. Numerical uncertainty for the alignment and cross-model patching results is not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results omitted. Other reported results concern internal folding mechanisms or feature steering rather than cross-model convergence.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size or capability, and no trend of alignment with scale. Only three fixed models are compared.
No vision or language models, and no paired image-caption data.
No same-architecture models trained from different seeds.
Stitching layers, relative representations and unpaired-data mapping are not tested. Paired residue-pair correspondences are required. Only pairwise (not sequence) representations are mapped.
No matching of individual neurons, SAE features or circuits across models. Charge and distance are probed separately in each model, not matched across models.
No systematic variation of similarity-measure settings, input sets or out-of-distribution data. Only a shuffled-control comparison of alignment methods (App. M.1) is reported.

Completeness is not measured against scale. There is no test of whether shared training data or objectives explain the alignment. The authors attribute pairing differences to architectural lineage but do not test this.

missing.what: Alignment-method comparison under shuffled correspondences. Ridge and CCA reach shuffled R2 of about 0.1–0.25, so they fit marginal statistics. Whitened Procrustes is near the about −1 floor. This shows apparent alignment depends on the map class.
Small positive R2 at blocks 0–5 for OpenFold→ESMFold and Boltz-1→ESMFold. The authors attribute it to positional-embedding structure, and it does not translate into successful patching.
Separate main-text values: Boltz-1→ESMFold Procrustes R2 ≈ 0.75 and patching peak near 10%. OpenFold→ESMFold patching is stated as near 15% here, versus 17% in App. M.

record.verdict_notes: V7 links were removed from all rows. The plateau the reader cited is across trunk depth, not model scale. Near-complete R2 (0.8–0.9) would, if anything, cut against V7's 'far from complete', but the study does not frame or test V7. Only three models are compared, and no uncertainty is given for the alignment or patching numbers. Released code covers ESMFold only.

versions.untested_parts: Does not sweep model size or capability, or test whether alignment rises with either.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
No comparison across random initializations or tests of shared features/subspaces across seeds.

Tests linear alignment and cross-model pairwise-state substitution among three protein-folding models; does not test stitching layers, relative representations, unpaired-data mapping, or transfer across general-purpose models.
Does not test recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Uses multiple measures and alignment controls, but does not systematically test sensitivity to similarity-measure settings, alternative inputs, or out-of-distribution data.
Reports incomplete, plateauing alignment; does not determine whether shared data/objectives or a common model of reality cause the alignment.

rows.subject: ESMFold and OpenFold

rows.note: Similarity is high across middle and late blocks and concentrates near corresponding blocks.
rows.check: CKA is a similarity score, not a map. It supports V4 only together with the Procrustes rows.

source_check.correct: CKA > 0.8 in middle and late blocks; state=cannot_determine for V4 from this measure alone. Linear mappability is established by the separate Procrustes results.
source_check.problem: CKA measures similarity and cannot independently establish V4 interchangeability.

rows.subject: ESMFold and OpenFold
rows.operation_detail: Fit whitened Procrustes projections between corresponding pairwise representations and evaluated test R2.
rows.note: Alignment rises from poor block-0 alignment and plateaus in later blocks; it is substantial but not complete.
rows.check: R2 ≈ 0.9 in both directions against a near-floor shuffled control is near-complete linear recoverability, so the state should be observed, not partial. The V7 link should be dropped. The 'plateau' is across trunk depth (blocks 5–15 onward), not across scale. A near-complete R2 does not show alignment staying far from complete.

relation.reason: Its own Procrustes and cross-model patching experiments directly test V4.

tranche.reason: The study tests linear alignment and causal substitution in protein-folding trunks, extending representation convergence to a new setting.

source_check.notes: The source is arXiv:2602.06020v3. Preserve both conflicting shuffled-control accounts and both OpenFold→ESMFold peak estimates; the text does not resolve them. Functional evidence concerns local motif induction, not preservation of overall folding accuracy.

statements.correction: ESMFold↔OpenFold test R² ≈ 0.9; OpenFold↔Boltz-1 test R² ≈ 0.8–0.9 at middle/late blocks. These measure mapped correspondence. Code release covers ESMFold experiments; uncertainty is reported for other experiments, with none stated for these alignment estimates.
OpenFold→ESMFold induction peaks near 15% in Section 6 or 17% in Appendix M; ESMFold self-patching peaks near 22%. Cross-model patching succeeds in the late-block window. V4 label=limits_scope.
statements.problem: The protein numbers and matched ESMFold baseline are correct, but this study shows reduced functional transfer rather than absent transfer; its result warrants limits_scope rather than challenges.

statements.correction: High protein-representation projection R² coexists with reduced hairpin-induction success relative to matched ESMFold self-patching.
